jobs.title: THE RENDER WEEK · The town loads
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: comic strip panel, black brush-pen ink line with muddy early-2000s digital flat colors, rubbery kinetic linework, mid-2000s webcomic look, limited palette, slightly misregistered fills. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 28, thin man, hunched, unshaven, tired bloodshot eyes, ink on his right knuckle; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. WOOD usually wears black hoodie open over a faded band tee; the brown chore coat outdoors; dark jeans. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: BACKUP. The strip: A science-fiction week the papers declined: the town as a render in progress. Monday: the seawall drawn in wireframe, then the flats, then the shack, each panel a little more solid, a progress bar under each, and Wood and the dog on the bench fully drawn from the first panel, waiting for the town to finish. It doesn't, by Friday. Panel 1: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a seawall and bay drawn as phosphor-green wireframe with a thin man and a small dog on a bench drawn solid, a thin progress bar drawn beneath the panel partly filled (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 2: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a seawall half-shaded emerging from wireframe with a man and a dog on a bench, a thin progress bar drawn beneath the panel partly filled fuller (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 3: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a solid seawall beside a bay still drawn as a green grid with a wireframe gull landing on the wall, a thin progress bar drawn beneath the panel partly filled (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Panel 4: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a thin man speaking to a small dog on a bench beside a green grid of water, a thin progress bar drawn beneath the panel partly filled stuck (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). No text, no lettering, no speech balloons, no signature; leave clean space in each panel where balloons would go. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_26 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_main_street shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @wood_26 for the character Wood at 24-31; @loc_main_street for the setting.
